newsitem.title: UK: "Very unlikely" UK will join EMU in 1999-Rifkind.
newsitem.headline: "Very unlikely" UK will join EMU in 1999-Rifkind.

text.p: British foreign secretary Malcolm Rifkind said on Thursday it was "very unlikely" that Britain would join a single currency in January 1999.

Rifkind, speaking after a cabinet meeting, told reporters: "As the Chancellor pointed out and as the cabinet concluded, it is unlikely that circumstances would lead to us wishing to join a single currency in January 1999.
"The crucial requirement is always the national interest and that is something we would put at the head of our consideration of this national issue."
Clarke told the reporters outside Major's Downing Street office: "It is unlikely in my opinion we would start EMU on January 1. It's not impossible but it's unlikely that they will.
"I think eventually that date will slip. But meanwhile we wouldn't join ourselves if anybody allowed the timetable to dominate common sense and went rushing ahead on a non-convergent basis.
"We would not contemplate possible joining on that basis ... when the time comes we will exercise our judgement one way or another." -- London Newsroom +44-171-542-7768
